recap.text: The S&P 500 declined 0.37% on Tuesday (and is down 0.59% for the week) as hotter-than-expected CPI inflation data sparked concerns over potential Federal Reserve rate hikes and drove Treasury yields sharply higher. Market sentiment was heavily weighed down by Information Technology, where a 5.5% plunge in Nvidia exacerbated pressure on high-multiple growth stocks. In contrast, value and defensive sectors outperformed, with Financials leading gains (+0.52%) on wider net interest margin expectations, while Energy (+0.44%) staged a late-session bounce despite crude oil sliding to multi-month lows on easing Middle East tensions.

items.SPY: The S&P 500 fell 0.37% as hotter-than-expected CPI data reignited Fed rate-hike fears and pushed Treasury yields higher, compounding weakness in heavyweight tech shares.
items.XLK: Technology dropped 1.15% (and is down 4.31% on the week) as soaring bond yields pressured high-valuation growth stocks and Nvidia tumbled 5.5% amid an analyst downgrade and a CEO scandal.
items.XLC: Communication Services rose 0.37% to extend its weekly advance to 6.23%, buoyed by resilient digital advertising sentiment and positive earnings reports across media and ad-tech names.
items.XLY: Consumer Discretionary ticked up 0.03%, holding ground despite higher bond yields as investors weighed recent solid jobs data against inflation pressures on consumer spending.
items.XLP: Consumer Staples gained 0.15% as market participants rotated into defensive, non-cyclical dividend payers amidst broader equity volatility and inflation uncertainty.
items.XLF: Financials led all sectors with a 0.52% gain, capitalizing on surging Treasury yields and elevated rate expectations that support bank lending margins.
items.XLV: Health Care added 0.29%, continuing its strong monthly rally (+10.58%) as investors sought defensive, non-discretionary cash flows during a tech-led market pullback.
items.XLI: Industrials slipped 0.09%, weighed down by broader macro concerns over stubborn inflation and the negative impact of higher borrowing costs on capital expenditure.
items.XLB: Materials fell 0.17% amid pressure on base metal prices and broader commodity sensitivity to rising interest rates and inflation data.
items.XLE: Energy rebounded 0.44% late in the day after a rough week (-6.70%), even as crude oil prices retreated toward two-month lows following signs of de-escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.
items.XLU: Utilities dipped 0.14% as surging Treasury yields diminished the relative appeal of bond-proxy dividend yields, dampening recent momentum in power and nuclear plays.
items.XLRE: Real Estate slipped 0.13% due to its heightened sensitivity to borrowing costs, as surging yields and hot CPI readings weighed on property financing expectations.

items.headline: Nvidia Shares Slump as Board Launches Probe into CEO Jensen Huang
items.profile: NVIDIA Corporation is a leading US semiconductor company and the world's dominant designer of accelerated computing hardware and software for AI.
items.what_happened: Nvidia shares dropped over 4% after the board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following an admitted relationship, deepening a selloff that erased an $1.84 trillion valuation lead. The decline allowed Microsoft to briefly overtake Nvidia as the world's second-most valuable company for the first time since June 2025.
items.why_it_matters: Sudden leadership and governance risks at the semiconductor industry's primary AI bellwether create significant uncertainty for the entire tech sector and chip supply chain.

items.headline: CoreWeave Tops Q3 Estimates and Reports $133 Billion Backlog
items.profile: CoreWeave is a specialized US cloud computing infrastructure provider focused on high-performance GPU compute for artificial intelligence workloads.
items.what_happened: CoreWeave posted third-quarter financial results that beat Wall Street forecasts, reporting smaller-than-anticipated cash burn despite widening year-over-year net losses. The company revealed that its business backlog reached $133 billion, sending its shares up 2.6% in after-hours trading.
items.why_it_matters: The massive order backlog demonstrates durable enterprise and hyperscaler commitment to dedicated AI cloud infrastructure despite broader tech market volatility.

items.headline: AMD Jumps 13% on Google AI Chip Deal and Doubling Data Center Sales
items.profile: Advanced Micro Devices is a major US semiconductor firm designing microprocessors, graphics processors, and AI accelerators for data centers and personal computing.
items.what_happened: AMD stock jumped 13.3% after securing an AI chip supply agreement with Google and receiving a Wall Street analyst price target upgrade. The company's data center revenue nearly doubled year-over-year, driving a 25% outperformance relative to Nvidia over two trading sessions.
items.why_it_matters: Hyperscaler adoption of AMD's silicon confirms that cloud providers are actively seeking secondary chip sources, loosening Nvidia's near-monopoly on data center accelerators.

items.headline: Rackspace Raises Full-Year Revenue Guidance on Strong Public Cloud Consumption
items.profile: Rackspace Technology is a US-based multicloud IT services provider delivering cloud management, infrastructure, and application solutions.
items.what_happened: Rackspace delivered third-quarter revenue of $609 million and lifted its full-year top-line guidance following stronger-than-expected Public Cloud usage. The company maintained its profit outlook while presenting an investment roadmap to expand AI computing capacity through 2027.
items.why_it_matters: The guidance increase highlights healthy underlying enterprise cloud utilization and suggests hybrid cloud services are capturing growing spillover demand from enterprise AI initiatives.

items.headline: IREN Reports 182% Sequential Jump in AI Cloud Revenue to $200 Million
items.profile: IREN Limited is a next-generation data center operator and AI cloud infrastructure provider originally established in Australia.
items.what_happened: IREN reported that AI cloud revenue surged 182% quarter-over-quarter to $200 million in its fiscal first quarter of 2027. Despite JPMorgan initiating coverage with a Buy rating on the back of the results, the company's shares fell approximately 4% to around $21.
items.why_it_matters: The triple-digit sequential growth demonstrates that specialized data center operators are successfully converting built-out high-performance computing capacity into immediate AI cloud revenues.
